title: Lavender infusion for nervous tension
subtitle: A gentle calming tea of Lavandula angustifolia for nervous tension and mild anxiety
excerpt: Lavender infusion is a hot tea of dried Lavandula angustifolia flowers steeped for 8 minutes, taken for nervous tension, mild anxiety, and the restless, agitated feeling of an overstimulated day. A gentle relaxant nervine from European herbal tradition. The linalool and linalyl acetate in the flowers carry into the steam and act on GABA receptors to produce a mild calming effect. One to two cups in the afternoon or at bedtime.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), lavender entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Lavandula angustifolia Miller, flos (2012, EMA/HMPC/143183/2010), open access.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried lavender flowers store 12 months in a sealed tin. Brew each cup fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb that gently reduces nervous system excitability without strong sedation, producing a calming, grounding effect rather than drowsiness. Lavender is a classic relaxant nervine; it eases tension without the strong sleep-promoting action of valerian or hops.

, taken in the afternoon for an agitated, overactive day, or in the early evening before bed. The flavour is floral and faintly sweet. Best drunk in small amounts rather than large mugs.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: dried lavender flowers (Lavandula angustifolia, not lavender essential oil)

content.text: Place 1 teaspoon of dried lavender flowers in a teapot or cup. Pour 200 ml of just-boiled water over the flowers. Cover and steep for 8 minutes.
Strain into a cup and drink warm. A small amount of honey may be added. Sip slowly.
One cup in the afternoon or early evening on days of elevated tension. For sustained nervous tension over several weeks, one cup daily for 4 weeks before reassessing.
Dried lavender flowers store 12 months in a sealed tin away from light. Brew each cup fresh.
When not to use this remedy

See a doctor for anxiety that is persistent or disabling. Also see a doctor for anxiety that comes with panic attacks, avoidance, or low mood. Lavender infusion is a gentle daily drink, not a treatment for anxiety disorders.
